newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A shares rise on futures crackdown talk.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares rise on futures crackdown talk.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index closed higher on Friday on buying triggered in part by rumours that Beijing would raise trading margin requirements on commodities futures trading, analysts said.
The rumours made investors believe that hot money would flow out of the futures market and into equities, they said. Officials declined comment.

The A share index rose 7.34 points or 2.66 percent to 282.91, with turnover rising to 6.06 billion yuan from 4.15 billion on Thursday. The composite index firmed 6.54 points, or 2.51 percent, to 266.85.

The B share index rose 0.22 point, or 0.24 percent, to 89.58 on turnover of HK$14.86 million, compared with Thursday's HK$10.26 million. Trading was concentrated on several large-cap issues, analysts said.
On the B share market, Gujing Distillery rose HK$0.01 to HK$5.62 on the day's heaviest trade of 557,100 shares. Guangdong Electric Power rose HK$0.01 to HK$5.40 on trading of 332,200 shares.
Television maker Huafa was the best performer, up HK$0.10, or 6.25 percent, to HK$1.70 on thin volume of 11,800 shares.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen was up HK$0.13 at HK$2.53 and real estate developer Hannan Pearl River was HK$0.07 higher at HK$1.84. Konka firmed HK$0.20, or 3.05 percent, to HK$6.75.
Chiwan Petroleum fell HK$0.24 to HK$3.30 and was the biggest loser.

On the A share market, Gujing Distillery, which listed 18 million class A shares in Shenzhen on Friday, closed the session at 23.00 yuan on active trade of 12.91 million shares, against its offer price of 8.48 yuan. The rise was due to speculative demand and Gujing's solid earnings record, brokers said.
